readingInstruction: Read Mark 1:1-45. Mark begins with no birth story and no prologue. Notice how quickly the scenes move, and how often the word “immediately” appears. Read it in one sitting if you can, to feel the pace.
settingTheScene: Mark is the shortest and probably the earliest of the four Gospels. Early Christians said it was written by John Mark, a companion of Peter, and that it reflects Peter’s preaching in Rome. It was written for a church that was suffering, and it presents Jesus as the strong Son of God who is also the suffering servant. Mark uses the word “immediately” (or “at once”) over forty times. Things happen quickly. There is almost no talk, and much action.
observation: “The beginning of the gospel of Jesus Christ, the Son of God” (1:1).
“And when he came up out of the water, immediately he saw the heavens being torn open and the Spirit descending on him like a dove” (1:10).
“The time is fulfilled, and the kingdom of God is at hand; repent and believe in the gospel” (1:15).
“Follow me, and I will make you become fishers of men” (1:17).
“And they were astonished at his teaching, for he taught them as one who had authority, and not as the scribes” (1:22).
“And rising very early in the morning, while it was still dark, he departed and went out to a desolate place, and there he prayed” (1:35).
“Moved with pity, he stretched out his hand and touched him and said to him, I will; be clean” (1:41).
“See that you say nothing to anyone” (1:44).
interpretation:
Mark’s first sentence is his title: “The beginning of the gospel of Jesus Christ, the Son of God.” Gospel means good news, the announcement of a victory. Mark tells us at once who Jesus is, though the people in the story will take most of the book to find out.

John the Baptist appears in the wilderness, as Isaiah promised, and says that one more powerful is coming. Jesus is baptized, and Mark says the heavens are “torn open,” a strong word, as the Spirit descends and the Father says, “You are my beloved Son; with you I am well pleased.” Immediately the Spirit drives him into the wilderness, where he is tempted by Satan for forty days. Mark gives the temptation in two verses. The battle between the Son of God and the powers of darkness has begun.

Then Jesus comes to Galilee: “The time is fulfilled, and the kingdom of God is at hand; repent and believe in the gospel.” This is the heart of his message. The long-awaited reign of God is arriving in his person. He calls Simon and Andrew, James and John, and they leave their nets at once.

In the synagogue in Capernaum, he teaches with authority, unlike the scribes, who quoted other rabbis. A man with an unclean spirit cries out, “I know who you are, the Holy One of God.” Jesus silences the demon and casts it out. The crowd is amazed. He heals Peter’s mother-in-law, and by evening the whole town is at the door. Yet early the next morning he withdraws to pray. His power flows from communion with the Father.

A leper kneels before him and says, “If you will, you can make me clean.” Moved with pity, Jesus stretches out his hand and touches him, something no one would do, and says, “I will; be clean.” The unclean person is made clean without making Jesus unclean. Then he commands the man to say nothing and to go to the priest. But the man tells everyone. This is the first appearance of a pattern in Mark that scholars call the Messianic secret: Jesus often silences demons and those he heals. We will return to why.
connection: Isaiah 40:3 and Malachi 3:1 are the prophecies Mark quotes at the start. Psalm 2:7 and Isaiah 42:1 stand behind the voice from heaven. Daniel 7 and Isaiah 52:7 are the background to the kingdom of God. Leviticus 13 and 14 give the laws of leprosy. 1 Peter 5:13 mentions Mark as Peter’s son in the faith. Acts 12:12 and Colossians 4:10 mention John Mark. Romans 1:16 says the gospel is the power of God for salvation.
application:
Read the chapter aloud quickly. How does the pace affect you?

Hear “repent and believe in the gospel” as a daily call, not a once-only event.

Like Jesus, find a quiet place early in the day to pray before the day’s demands begin.
prayerPrompts: Repent and believe in the good news, in your own words.
Thank Jesus that the kingdom is at hand.
Ask him to help you follow him immediately.
